text:
MPC rose modestly today, continuing a sharp recovery over the past week after dropping 6.76% in the two weeks prior. The stock has climbed $42 (roughly 11%) since November 6th, driven largely by refinery fundamentals improving: US refineries are running at 95.2% capacity, and heating oil prices have spiked 59% year-over-year due to winter demand and tight supply. That pricing power benefits refiners like Marathon, which profit when the gap between crude input costs and refined product sales widens.

However, headwinds are building. Russian crude production has rebounded sharply—the IEA reported output at 8.73 million barrels per day in October—pushing global oil markets back into surplus. That oversupply dynamic typically pressures crude prices and narrows refiner margins, which may explain why today's gain is modest despite the heating oil strength. The stock's recovery could stall if crude supplies continue to ease and refined product demand weakens heading into winter.
